newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rutges wins NCA ground handling contract at Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: Rutges wins NCA ground handling contract at Frankfurt.

text.p: Dutch airfreight trucking company Rutges BV said it has won a ground handling contract for Nippon Cargo Airlines a at Frankfurt airport.

The contract covers consolidation freight handling, documentation, road distribution to and from German airports and regular airfreight trucking between Frankfurt and Amsterdam, a Rutges statement said.
No details of the financial value of the contract were given.
Rutges already trucks NCA airfreight from Germany to Amsterdam, where the all-freight airline has five weekly freighter flights to Japan.
Rutges will handle the freight at a new 3,000 square metre terminal at Frankfurt airport's Cargo City South freight facility which is due to open in March.

At a signing ceremony in the new terminal, Eiji Tanaka, NCA vice-president sales and marketing, said the Japanese cargo airline now had the right partner for long-term reliable handling and the new contract would deepen its long-standing relationship with Rutges.
Rutges managing director Nico Leyer said the new terminal offered room for expansion and he hoped other airlines would now follow NCA to Cargo City South.
Rutges said it has 18 offices in seven European countries, employs more than 450 staff and operates more than 200 trucks. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
